title: For long-horizon work, persist state as structured notes outside the context window
statement: On tasks that exceed one context window, have the agent write structured notes to durable storage (a NOTES.md, a to-do list, a ledger) and read them back after a reset, so progress and decisions survive compaction.
rationale: Working memory is bounded and lossy across resets. Externalizing state to files gives persistent memory at minimal overhead and lets the agent resume multi-hour tasks coherently.
applies_when: Tasks spanning many tool calls or multiple sessions
Work must survive a context reset or compaction
not_when: Short tasks that complete well within one window
how: Have the agent maintain a notes/progress file as it works
Reload the notes into context after a reset instead of relying on retained history
Keep the notes structured (decisions, open problems, next step) rather than free narrative
check: After a simulated context reset, can the agent resume correctly from its own notes alone? If not, its memory is not durable.
failure_if_absent: An agent forgets decisions and repeats or contradicts earlier work once the original context is summarized away.

evidence.title: Anthropic - Effective context engineering (structured note-taking)
evidence.quote: your custom agent maintaining a NOTES.md file, this simple pattern allows the agent to track progress across complex tasks, maintaining critical context and dependencies that would otherwise be lost across dozens of tool calls
